parsed_response.reasoning: Verifiable in the diff: in save(), props.category_id is captured at click time from this.get('categoryId'), but the success callback later calls host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))) — re-reading the chooser's current value after the request resolves. The template only disables the save/cancel buttons (disabled=cantSave / host.isSaving) during the request; {{category-chooser value=categoryId}} remains enabled, so a user can change the category while a save is in flight, and the UI will then show the newly selected category even though the server persisted the old one. A real, if minor, correctness race introduced by this new code.

judged_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — [P2/100] "host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));" Changing the still-enabled category chooser from A to B while a save of A is in flight makes the success callback display B as saved even though the server persisted A; rebuttal: the save and cancel buttons are disabled during the request; survives because: the category chooser remains enabled and the callback reads its current value instead of the saved request or response.

record.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — [P2/100] "host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));" Changing the still-enabled category chooser from A to B while a save of A is in flight makes the success callback display B as saved even though the server persisted A; rebuttal: the save and cancel buttons are disabled during the request; survives because: the category chooser remains enabled and the callback reads its current value instead of the saved request or response.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the category chooser remains enabled during save, but looking at the template (embeddable-host.hbs line 10), the cancel button is disabled with 'disabled=host.isSaving'. However, the category-chooser itself is NOT disabled during save - only the buttons are. But the finding's core claim is wrong: the callback uses 'this.get('categoryId')' which reads the component's categoryId property that was set in props before the save (line 33: 'props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')'). The save() call captures the categoryId at the time of the request. The success callback then uses the same categoryId value. While there's a theoretical race condition if the user could change the category during save, the finding incorrectly states the rebuttal is wrong - the save button IS disabled (line 9: 'disabled=cantSave' where cantSave includes isSaving). The category chooser not being disabled is a valid concern, but the finding's reasoning about the callback reading 'current value instead of saved request' is incorrect - it reads the same categoryId that was sent.
